scope: Complete source review of LLVM InstructionCost.h and InstructionCost.cpp at the pinned revision
insights: Validity is a separate cost state; invalid is not merely a very large valid price. LLVM explicitly advises against using its Invalid state for unknown cost. Ink should preserve separate eligibility/proof and observation-completeness gates.

Saturating arithmetic prevents overflow from making expensive transformations appear cheap. Ink already bounds source counters and validates nonnegative finite physical prices; no duplicate numeric framework added.

This LLVM revision uses internal quarter-unit granularity. Relative instruction costs are not nanoseconds and cannot be copied into Ink target prices without target/boundary calibration. Raw internal values, public integer conversion and formatting use different scales.
Printing preserves quarter-unit fractions and handles minimum signed values through unsigned magnitude arithmetic. Diagnostics must not silently present truncated values as exact calibrated prices.
Validity propagation and unit discipline are general mechanisms worth retaining; neither replaces source equivalence proofs or measured held-out profitability.
followup: InstructionCost call-site usage, including map callbacks receiving the internal value, still needs separate audit; these two complete file reviews do not cover all LLVM cost consumers.
performance: No new performance measurement or claim
